date_basis: 2026-08-20 session date; no wall-clock timestamp asserted

revision.reason: The superseded draft measured whole-module LUT6 counts after `flatten`, which lets ABC re-synthesize across the S-box boundary and therefore cannot measure marginal keying cost at all.
revision.observed_failure: offset mapped to 158 LUT6 while the logically identical offset_alt mapped to 187 LUT6, with 1792/1792 functional checks passing in both cases; the flattened flow also reported affine (135) as cheaper than offset (158), which is structurally impossible for a marginal-cost reading
revision.prior_receipt_status: no receipt was generated under the superseded preregistration; the harness failed closed with INVALID_COST_HARNESS
revision.correction: Synthesis now preserves hierarchy so the shared S-box is never re-optimized against the wrapper, and the graded metric is the top module's local cell count, which is exactly the keying overhead.
revision.unchanged_thresholds: The P4 (>=4x) and P6 (<=32) thresholds are carried over verbatim from the superseded draft so that correcting the methodology cannot be confused with moving the goalposts.

purpose: Replace the hand gate-count estimates in directives/e256-hardware-architecture.md with measured LUT6 synthesis cost for one rotor lane realized four ways, so that H3 (demote rotor keying to XOR-offset conjugation) is decided by measurement rather than assertion.

authorization.contract_hash_preimage: all bytes strictly between the unique start and end marker strings, including their surrounding newlines but excluding both marker strings
authorization.allowed: preregistered cost-estimation research on non-production RTL
blocked: security-bit, timing-closure, power, or side-channel claim

predecessor.inherited_result: Wide state structurally retained for attack only; fixed-AES comparator reached identical structural bounds, so the keyed rotor namespace has no demonstrated advantage and its cost is the open question.

questions.text: What is the measured marginal LUT6 cost of each rotor keying scheme over an unkeyed fixed S-box lane holding the S-box description constant?
Is the programmable-affine marginal cost materially larger than the XOR-offset marginal cost, as H3 assumes?
Does realizing the identical rotor function as a runtime-loaded 256-entry lookup cost more logic than the equivalent netlist, as H1 assumes?
Is the LUT6 metric stable against a logically equivalent but differently written description?

toolchain_contract.version_binding: Synthesis results are tool-dependent, so the recorded yosys and iverilog version strings enter the deterministic payload; a different toolchain must fail --check loudly rather than silently compare different numbers.

synthesis_contract.script: read_verilog <rtl>; hierarchy -check -top <module>; proc; memory; opt; techmap; opt; dffunmap; zinit -all; abc -lut 6; opt_clean; check -assert; stat; ltp -noff
synthesis_contract.script_provenance: same pass order as the existing Mulein bounded LUT6 lane in the Makefile, with `flatten` deliberately removed
synthesis_contract.flatten_prohibited: `flatten` must not appear. Flattening lets ABC re-synthesize the shared S-box together with the keying logic, which destroys the structural boundary the marginal measurement depends on and makes the metric description-sensitive.
synthesis_contract.target: generic 6-input LUT mapping by ABC; not a vendor architecture and not place-and-route
synthesis_contract.keying_lut6_metric: the local $lut count reported by stat for the top module, which excludes submodules and is therefore exactly the keying overhead added around the shared S-box; absent means zero
synthesis_contract.shared_sbox_lut6_metric: the local $lut count reported by stat for e256h_aes_sbox in the same run
synthesis_contract.depth_metric: length reported by ltp -noff for the top module in the mapped netlist
synthesis_contract.graded_quantity: keying_lut6, compared across variants; the shared S-box cost is reported for context and is identical wherever an S-box is instantiated
synthesis_contract.invocation: one yosys process per variant with -Q, no shared state between variants

key_material.derivation: reuse the frozen E256-W model KDF exactly, so the measured lane matches the certified construction
key_material.matrix_in: first rank-8 result of PurposeStream(rotor_key, base || ASCII '/matrix/in/attempt/' || u16be(attempt)).read(8)
key_material.matrix_out: first rank-8 result of PurposeStream(rotor_key, base || ASCII '/matrix/out/attempt/' || u16be(attempt)).read(8)
key_material.constants: PurposeStream(rotor_key, base || ASCII '/constants').read(2); byte 0 is c_in, byte 1 is c_out
key_material.offset_parameters: p_in = c_in and p_out = c_out, so the offset lane is exactly the affine lane with both matrices set to identity
key_material.matrix_packing: row r occupies bits [8*r+7 : 8*r] of the 64-bit port, matching the frozen row-order convention where output bit r is parity(row_r AND x)
key_material.table_contents: the 256-byte forward table of the affine lane at the same parameters, packed little-endian as tbl[8*x+7 : 8*x], so the table lane computes an identical function by lookup

variants.function: y = SBOX(x XOR p_in) XOR p_out
identical to offset, written with per-bit loops instead of byte expressions
y = L_out(SBOX(L_in(x) XOR c_in)) XOR c_out with runtime matrices
y = tbl[x], runtime-loaded 256-entry lookup computing the same function as affine

shared_sbox.description: one 256-entry truth-table description of the AES S-box shared by every S-box-bearing variant
shared_sbox.rationale: holding the S-box description constant makes the difference between variants the keying overhead, which is the quantity under test
shared_sbox.explicit_limitation: this is a truth-table description optimized by ABC, not a tower-field or depth-optimized S-box circuit, so its absolute cost must not be compared to published gate-equivalent S-box figures

functional_verification.requirement: every variant must match the frozen Python model on all 256 inputs before any cost number is interpreted
functional_verification.vectors: generated from the frozen key material and compared in an Icarus Verilog testbench
equivalence_obligations: offset output equals affine output when both matrices are the identity
table output equals affine output on all 256 inputs
offset_alt output equals offset output on all 256 inputs

predictions.rationale: a wire-through must not consume logic; a nonzero count means the flow inflates trivial designs and no cost number is trustworthy
eight independent 2-input XORs; a larger count means the flow is not mapping simple logic sensibly

predictions.statement: offset_alt keying_lut6 and depth equal offset keying_lut6 and depth exactly
predictions.rationale: if a logically identical rewrite changes the metric, the metric is description noise and the comparison is void; this control already rejected one methodology

predictions.statement: fixed keying_lut6 is exactly 0 and its shared_sbox_lut6 is greater than 0
predictions.rationale: confirms the hierarchy boundary is intact, so the shared S-box cost is attributed to the submodule and never to keying

predictions.statement: affine keying_lut6 is at least 4x offset keying_lut6
predictions.rationale: this is the measurable core of H3; failure removes the cost justification for demoting programmable affine keying
predictions.threshold_provenance: carried over verbatim from the superseded draft

predictions.statement: table keying_lut6 is strictly greater than the shared S-box cost
predictions.rationale: supports H1 by showing a runtime lookup is not a cheap way to obtain a keyed rotor in logic
two byte XORs should be near-free; a larger figure would weaken H3 even if P4 holds
predictions.threshold_provenance: carried over verbatim from the superseded draft

predictions.statement: offset depth is strictly less than affine depth
predictions.rationale: H3 should reduce logic levels as well as area; a latency win is part of the claim being tested

hard_rejection_rules: Refuse the receipt if the architecture contract hash, this preregistration hash, the predecessor payload digest, the AES S-box hash, or either pinned tool version drifts.
Refuse the receipt if any variant fails functional verification on all 256 inputs or any equivalence obligation fails.
Refuse the receipt if any validity_control prediction (P1, P2, P3, P7) fails.
Refuse the receipt if the synthesis script contains a flatten pass.
Refuse the receipt if the executed variant ID set does not equal the frozen variant ID set.
Do not select a round count, declare a production keying scheme, or infer security from any cost number.

interpretation.internal_invalid_status: INVALID_COST_HARNESS; never emitted or accepted as the canonical receipt

decision_table.condition: contract, coverage, functional, or validity-control failure
decision_table.action: exit nonzero and refuse canonical receipt write/check

interpretation.scope: one combinational byte lane only; the 32-lane round, register budget, schedule, and mode are not measured here
interpretation.next: A supported result promotes H3 from proposal to measured default and licenses the H4/H5 structural re-certification. It does not license production RTL or a round count.

non_claims: LUT6 counts are yosys/ABC generic mapping artifacts, not vendor place-and-route, not gate equivalents, and not ASIC area.
No timing closure, Fmax, power, energy, TVLA, EM, or fault result is produced.
Constant-latency combinational logic is not side-channel resistance.
Only marginal keying cost is compared; the absolute S-box cost reflects a truth-table description, not an optimized tower-field circuit.
Keying cost is measured with hierarchy preserved. A flattened, globally optimized implementation will not reproduce these numbers, and the ratios are properties of this flow rather than of silicon.

LUT6 ratios do not transfer to ASIC gate equivalents; the hand estimate in the architecture record put programmable-affine wrappers at 3-5x an optimized tower-field S-box, which a 6-LUT fabric does not reproduce.
Register and parameter-storage budgets under H2 are not measured by this gate.
A cheaper lane is not a stronger lane; no structural or security certificate is affected by any figure here.
This RTL is a non-production cost model and is not a specification, suite, profile, or fixture.
No C/H/N row, E256 finding, suite, profile, fixture, or release gate closes here, and reviewed standard AEAD remains mandatory for real data.

receipt_contract.checker: recompute frozen hashes, key material, vectors, functional verification, all syntheses, predictions, payload, and digest; require the validity gate to pass; compare the complete deterministic payload and digest byte-for-byte
receipt_contract.write: sorted indented UTF-8 JSON with final newline and atomic replacement
